CausalChain: Vitamin D treatment → Upregulation of miR‐375 → Suppression of c‐Myc expression → Reversal of EMT and reduction of cancer stemness → Enhanced sensitivity to mTOR inhibitors; Exosome‐mediated delivery of miR‐375 further amplifies this pathway → Synergistic effect in overcoming drug resistance in HCC.
Hypothesis: In hepatocellular carcinoma, combining vitamin D supplementation with engineered exosomes delivering miR‐375 mimics will synergistically reverse EMT and restore sensitivity to mTOR inhibitors by targeting c‐Myc and perturbing downstream pro‐survival and stemness pathways.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits frequent resistance to targeted therapies that is often linked to an epithelial‐to‐mesenchymal transition (EMT) and the enrichment of cancer stem cell features. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of microRNAs in modulating EMT and drug resistance, and exosome‐mediated delivery represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic hurdles. In particular, miR‐375 has emerged as a critical tumor suppressor in HCC by targeting the oncogene c‐Myc, whose downregulation is associated with reduced EMT and enhanced drug sensitivity. Vitamin D has also been shown to upregulate miR‐375, suggesting that its administration might potentiate responses to mTOR inhibitors such as everolimus. Here, we propose a novel therapeutic strategy combining vitamin D supplementation with engineered exosomes loaded with miR‐375 mimics to synergistically reverse EMT and restore drug sensitivity in HCC.
